title: Equivalence of slice diagrams is detected on relative right-cone diagrams
statement:
Use the small simplicial sets, quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets and equivalence edges of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a small quasicategory, $y$ a vertex, and $J$ any small simplicial set in the same fixed universe. Let $S_y$ have $n$-simplices $\sigma:\Delta^{n+1}\to\mathcal C$ with last vertex $y$, and operators given by extending $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$ to $\alpha^+:[m+1]\to[n+1]$ with $\alpha^+(m+1)=n+1$. Define the right cone $J^{\triangleright}=J\star\Delta^0$ by adjoining a last vertex $*$: besides the simplices of $J$ and the constant simplices at $*$, its simplices are concatenations of a simplex of $J$ and a nonempty constant simplex at $*$, with operators given by restricting the two ordered blocks. Thus $(\Delta^n)^{\triangleright}=\Delta^{n+1}$.
For a simplicial map $e:J\to S_y$, let $F_e:J^{\triangleright}\to\mathcal C$ be the corresponding cone diagram: for each simplex $a:\Delta^n\to J$ its restriction along $a^{\triangleright}:\Delta^{n+1}\to J^{\triangleright}$ is the simplex $e_n(a)$; in particular $F_e(*)=y$. Put
$$\mathcal A_J=\operatorname{Fun}(J^{\triangleright},\mathcal C)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_*,\mathcal C}\{y\}.$$
Here an $r$-simplex in the strict fiber $\mathcal A_J$ is a map $J^{\triangleright}\times\Delta^r\to\mathcal C$ whose restriction to $\{*\}\times\Delta^r$ is constant at $y$. For any two simplicial maps $e_0,e_1:J\to S_y$, there exists an equivalence edge between $e_0,e_1$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(J,S_y)$ if and only if there exists an equivalence edge between $F_{e_0},F_{e_1}$ in $\mathcal A_J$. Equivalence edge has its inverse-and-two-triangle meaning, in both simplicial sets.

source.place: Lemma 4.6.4.25, conditions (1) and (2), specialized to K = Delta^0 and F = y. Read the statement and categorical-mapping-cylinder proof online 2026-10-16. This is a Kerodon tag, not Stacks Tag 01KV. Not archived under literature/.

proof.text: For every small simplicial set $L$, the definitions give a bijection between maps $e:L\to S_y$ and maps $F:L\star\Delta^0\to\mathcal C$ taking the apex to $y$. Explicitly, on a pure $L$-simplex $a\in L_n$ put $F(a)=d_{n+1}e_n(a)$, and on a pure apex simplex use the constant simplex at $y$. On a mixed $r$-simplex with initial block $a\in L_p$ and final nonempty apex block, use the pullback of $e_p(a)$ along the monotone map $[r]\to[p+1]$ which is the identity on the first $p+1$ vertices and sends the remaining vertices to $p+1$. Restricting an ordered block commutes with this formula, by the $\alpha^+$ operators of $S_y$; when the initial block disappears it gives the constant simplex at $y$. Conversely set $e_n(a)=F\circ(a\star\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^0})$ on $\Delta^{n+1}$. These two operations are inverse: every mixed simplex is a degeneracy in the apex block of one with a single final apex vertex. The formulas also show that the bijection commutes with precomposition by every map $L'\to L$.

source.place: Universal property of the join slice specialized to a point; explicit degreewise verification.

proof.text: The simplicial set $S_y$ is a quasicategory, without invoking the slice-arrow comparison that uses the present item. Indeed a horn $\Lambda_i^n\to S_y$, $0<i<n$, corresponds by the preceding formulas and facewise gluing to a map $\Lambda_i^n\star\Delta^0\to\mathcal C$. Restrict to the initial horn $\Lambda_i^n$ and fill it in $\mathcal C$. Adjoining this initial $n$-simplex to the prescribed joined horn gives a map from $\Lambda_i^{n+1}$: its faces with indices $j\ne i$, $j\leq n$, are the joined prescribed faces, and its last face is the just chosen simplex. Their intersections agree by construction. Since $0<i<n+1$, fill this second inner horn in $\mathcal C$. The filler has last vertex $y$ and so defines the required $n$-simplex in $S_y$.

source.place: Direct two-inner-horn proof of the quasicategory hypothesis in Lemma 4.6.4.25.

proof.text: Factor the fold map $J\amalg J\to J$ by the cofibration--trivial-fibration factorization of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure] as $J\amalg J\hookrightarrow\overline J\xrightarrow{\pi}J$. Let $s_0,s_1$ be its restrictions to the two copies. The factorization equation gives $\pi s_i=\operatorname{id}_J$, the first map is degreewise injective, and the trivial fibration $\pi$ is a categorical equivalence. Thus these data satisfy precisely the definition of a categorical mapping cylinder for $J$ relative to the empty subset in [lem-coef-relative-categorical-cylinder-criterion]. All objects remain small in the fixed universe, by the cited factorization statement.

source.place: Choice of a categorical mapping cylinder; Definition 4.6.3.3 (01K5), using the Joyal factorization.

proof.text: Put $B=J\star\Delta^0$, $A=\{*\}$, $\overline B=\overline J\star\Delta^0$, $s'_i=s_i\star\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^0}$ and $\pi'=\pi\star\operatorname{id}_{\Delta^0}$. The map $\pi'$ is a categorical equivalence by [lem-coef-join-preserves-categorical-equivalences], since $\pi$ and the identity are categorical equivalences. We have $\pi's'_i=\operatorname{id}_B$, and both sections agree on $A$. Moreover $B\amalg_A B\to\overline B$ is degreewise injective: on each pure $J$ summand or mixed summand it is the corresponding injection from one copy of $J_p$ into $\overline J_p$; the two images are disjoint because $J\amalg J\hookrightarrow\overline J$ is injective. Their only common summand is the pure apex, already identified in the gluing. Hence these joined data are a categorical mapping cylinder for $B$ relative to $A$, with exactly the hypotheses of [lem-coef-relative-categorical-cylinder-criterion].

source.place: The joined cylinder relative to the apex; Corollary 4.6.2.9 (01HW) and the degreewise injection check.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-relative-categorical-cylinder-criterion] with domain $J$, subset $\varnothing$, target $Q=S_y$ (a quasicategory by Step 2), and the cylinder of Step 3. It says that an equivalence edge between $e_0,e_1$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(J,S_y)$ exists exactly when there is $\overline e:\overline J\to S_y$ with $\overline e s_i=e_i$ for $i=0,1$.

source.place: Condition (1) reformulated as (1 prime), by Corollary 4.6.3.11 (01KD).

proof.text: Apply the same criterion with domain $B=J\star\Delta^0$, subset $A=\{*\}$, target $Q=\mathcal C$, common restriction $f_A(*)=y$, diagrams $F_{e_0},F_{e_1}$, and the cylinder of Step 4. The relative functor simplicial set in that criterion is exactly $\mathcal A_J$: in degree $r$ the restriction to $\{*\}\times\Delta^r$ is the constant simplex at $y$, with precisely the same operators. It follows that an equivalence edge between $F_{e_0},F_{e_1}$ in $\mathcal A_J$ exists exactly when there is $\overline F:\overline J\star\Delta^0\to\mathcal C$ with $\overline F s'_i=F_{e_i}$ for $i=0,1$. Any such extension already fixes the apex, since the apex belongs to each section image.

source.place: Condition (2) reformulated as (2 prime), in the strict relative diagram category, by 01KD.

proof.text: Use Step 1 for $L=\overline J$. It identifies the two extension conditions in Steps 5 and 6. In one direction $\overline e s_i=e_i$ implies $F_{\overline e}(s_i\star\operatorname{id})=F_{e_i}$ by the explicit precomposition formula. Conversely any $\overline F$ of Step 6 takes its apex to $y$, and so determines $\overline e$; restricting $\overline F$ along $s'_i$ and applying the inverse formula gives $\overline e s_i=e_i$. Combining the two equivalences of existence conditions proves the required if and only if, with equivalence edges throughout understood by their inverse and both triangle witnesses.

source.place: Final universal-property identification of (1 prime) and (2 prime).

lean.statement: theorem join_slice_diagram_equivalence_iff (C : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory C] (y : C _⦋0⦌) (J : SSet.{u}) (e₀ e₁ : J ⟶ rightVertexSlice C y) : AreNaturallyEquivalent e₀ e₁ ↔ ∃ f : (rightConeDiagramFiber C J y).toSSet _⦋1⦌, ((rightConeDiagramFiber C J y).toSSet.δ 1 f).val = diagramVertex (rightConeExtension y e₀) ∧ ((rightConeDiagramFiber C J y).toSSet.δ 0 f).val = diagramVertex (rightConeExtension y e₁) ∧ IsEquivalenceEdge (rightConeDiagramFiber C J y).toSSet f
